rows.name: Federal Reserve investment and trading rules for senior officials (FOMC, 2022)
rows.citation: FOMC rules adopted February 18, 2022 (effective May 1, 2022; notice and pre-clearance from July 1, 2022)
rows.regulator: Federal Open Market Committee / Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
rows.requires: Senior Federal Reserve officials (FOMC participants, Reserve Bank presidents, senior staff) may not hold single-company shares, sector funds, individual bonds, crypto, commodities, foreign currencies or derivatives, may not short sell or trade on margin; trades need 45 days notice, prior approval and a one-year holding period; no trading in periods of heightened market stress; prohibited holdings divested within 12 months.
rows.helps: Publish the pre-clearance log; disclose holdings on the annual OGE 278e; recuse where a holding is affected.

notice.quote: The rules will take effect on May 1, 2022, except that the requirements for advance notice and pre-clearance of transactions will take effect on July 1, 2022.

rows.name: IMF Central Bank Transparency Code (2020)
rows.citation: IMF Policy Paper No. 2020/038, approved by the IMF Executive Board July 2020
rows.regulator: International Monetary Fund (voluntary code for member central banks)
rows.requires: A voluntary framework by which a central bank discloses its governance, policies, operations, outcomes and official relations, assessed at core, expanded and comprehensive levels; replaces the 1999 Monetary and Financial Policies Transparency Code.
rows.helps: Publish the central bank law, decision-making rules, audited accounts, policy decisions with rationale, and the relationship with the government.

rows.name: Research security programs at covered institutions (NSPM-33 and the 2024 OSTP guidelines)
rows.citation: National Security Presidential Memorandum 33 (January 14, 2021); OSTP Guidelines for Research Security Programs at Covered Institutions (July 9, 2024); CHIPS and Science Act §10634
rows.regulator: White House OSTP; each federal research agency (NSF guidance effective October 2025)
rows.requires: Institutions receiving more than $50 million a year in federal science and engineering support must certify a research security program with four elements: cybersecurity, foreign travel security, research security training and export control training; agencies set the effective dates (institutions have up to 18 months after an agency plan takes effect).
rows.helps: Name the research security officer, publish the program, and disclose foreign support and affiliations in federal applications.

rows.name: California Political Reform Act of 1974 (conflicts of interest and disclosure)
rows.requires: Public officials disclose economic interests (Form 700), may not take part in decisions in which they have a financial interest, and campaign and lobbying money is reported publicly.

rows.name: Texas Government Code Chapter 572 (personal financial disclosure, standards of conduct, conflicts of interest)

rows.helps: File the personal financial statement by the deadline; disclose and abstain on conflicting matters.

rows.citation: 775 ILCS 5/2-102(L) as amended by P.A. 103-0804 (effective January 1, 2026)
